text:
alex.support: Heads-up — Acme (prod) filed a P2: p95 latency jumped from ~200ms to 1.6s starting ~09:15 UTC. They say traces show requests hitting eu-west-1 even though app region is us-west-2. Can we triage?

nate.support: +1. Support saw a cluster of 502/504 spikes too. Customer reported that only some endpoints are slow (generation API). I grabbed a trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d, sample request id: req_8f7e9.

jamie.sre: On it. Any headers or routing metadata available from the traces? We should check x-region / x-routing hints and the fallback logs on gateway.

alex.support: Pasted the important bits from their trace (redacted):
```
request_id: req_8f7e9
trace_id: trace-0a1b2c3d
x-client-region: us-west-2
x-edge-region: us-west-2
x-internal-region: eu-west-1
x-routing-reason: fallback_capacity_exhausted
```
They also have the raw curl they used against our API: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

maria.eng-runtime: That header `x-internal-region: eu-west-1` is the smoking gun — the request was proxied to eu-west. Two likely causes: 1) smart-router fallback to compatible model pool in eu-west due to us-west capacity exhausted, or 2) a mis-evaluated latency policy that prefers eu-west for that customer because of stale region affinity.

jamie.sre: I pulled gateway logs for the timeframe. There are ~1200 requests in a 2m window that got routed to eu-west-1 with routing_reason=fallback_capacity_exhausted. Our cluster manager reported pod pressure in us-west-2 at 09:13:42 UTC and set a temporary drain flag on one pool. Looks like autoscaler didn't spin up reserved nodes quickly enough.

alex.support: Customer claims they have reserved capacity and weren't expecting fallback. Could this be an auth/tenant mismatch where the customer’s dedicated pool wasn't honored?

maria.eng-runtime: Possible. Two checks: verify the customer's tenant_id->pool mapping in the control plane at the time, and confirm that the dedicated pool's healthcheck reported healthy. I see control-plane event: `pool_reserve_sync_delay` at 09:12:58 UTC for tenant acme-prod. That lines up.

nate.support: Customer also attached a packet capture showing SYN/ACK times that jump when the request is proxied cross-region — ~20ms -> ~210ms additional RTT. They're angry about extra egress cost and tail latency.

jamie.sre: Repro steps to validate internally: 1) run a looped single-token call from us-west infra with tenant header for acme-prod with 1000 reqs at 80% concurrency; 2) watch routing decisions in router service logs; 3) confirm fallback triggers when node_util > threshold. I'll kick off a small canary.

maria.eng-runtime: Also add a trace sampling that includes `route_decision` spans and `pool_selector` metadata. If we can capture the exact decision tree at the time we can see why it chose eu-west.

deploy-bot: deploy job #deploy-1123 started by jamie.sre — canary routing-telemetry v2 -> infra-canary (us-west-2)

jamie.sre: Canary findings: reproduced the fallback in ~10 minutes when we saturated the ded pool. Router logged: `selected_pool: eu-west-1-compatible-quant` with `reason: capacity_fallback` and `decision_path: prefer_low_cost_when_latency_ok`. That last flag is surprising — it should be gated behind customer_tier != dedicated. Looks like a policy eval bug.

alex.support: If policy incorrectly treats dedicated customers as standard, that explains the routing. Customer was billed for cross-region egress. Need to remediate and offer credits.

maria.eng-runtime: Quick mitigation steps: 1) Patch policy so dedicated pools are excluded from cross-region cost-based fallback (hotfix rolling to router); 2) Add emergency rule to prefer local pool for tenants with reserved capacity for next 24h; 3) Reconcile control-plane state to ensure pool_reserve_sync_delay alerts earlier.

jamie.sre: I've opened an internal incident (INC-2026-089) and assigned owners. Patch ready for review, will rollout to prod canary in 5m.

nate.support: I'll send the customer a summary: root cause = temporary control-plane delay + policy bug causing cost-based fallback to compatible pools in eu-west; impact = increased latency and egress charges; remediation = patching policy + credits + longer-term autoscaler tuning. Draft message ready, ping me for wording.

alex.support: Thanks — include the trace ids and the timeframe 09:12—09:20 UTC. Also offer a joint call if they want deeper logs. :hugging_face:

maria.eng-runtime: Postmortem action items I'm adding: - urgent: block cross-region fallbacks for dedicated tenants (P0) - medium: surface pool_reserve_sync_delay as an SLO alert - low: decrease autoscaler cooldown for reserved pools - verify routing telemetry captures `decision_path` for all sampled requests

jamie.sre: Patch rolled to canary and validating. I'll update this thread with rollback window and a link to the incident doc.

alex.support: Great work. Keep me posted before we close the incident.

nate.support: Sent customer the summary + credits proposal. They've accepted the credits and want the postmortem. Will coordinate schedule for the review.
